name: Anfinsen's Dogma
statement: A protein's native three-dimensional structure is determined entirely by its amino acid sequence.
statementAccent: determined entirely by its amino acid sequence
meaning: A protein does not need any external template or additional genetic information to reach its correctly folded, biologically active shape: the folding information is encoded fully in the linear order of amino acids. Under proper physiological conditions, the sequence alone specifies a unique, thermodynamically stable structure that is also kinetically reachable.
mechanism: Anfinsen framed this as a thermodynamic hypothesis: the native fold is the free-energy minimum accessible under physiological conditions, requiring uniqueness, marginal stability, and kinetic accessibility. He established it by denaturing ribonuclease A with urea and mercaptoethanol, then showing that on removal of the denaturants the unfolded chain spontaneously refolded into the correct disulfide-bonded structure and regained full activity, without any other cellular machinery present.

examples.text: Anfinsen’s 1961 experiment: denatured, reduced ribonuclease A, once denaturants were removed, spontaneously refolded in vitro and recovered its catalytic activity, showing sequence alone sufficed to specify structure.
AI systems such as AlphaFold predict accurate 3D protein structures directly from amino acid sequence alone, a practical validation of the principle that sequence encodes structure.

Energy-landscape theory (Bryngelson and Wolynes) formalised Anfinsen’s postulate by showing evolved sequences have "funnelled," minimally frustrated landscapes guiding them reliably to one native energy minimum.

whyItMatters: The dogma underlies the entire logic of molecular biology’s sequence-to-structure-to-function paradigm and justifies computational structure prediction from sequence alone. It also set the conceptual foundation that later challenges (chaperones, prions, fold-switching proteins) had to be reconciled against.
limits: Some proteins require chaperones to fold efficiently in the crowded cell, though chaperones mainly prevent aggregation rather than dictate the final fold. Misfolding diseases (prions, amyloids in Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s) show alternative, sometimes more stable, conformations can occur, and a minority of proteins (roughly 0.5–4%) are fold-switching, adopting more than one native structure.
misreadings: It is sometimes misread as claiming folding happens with no cellular assistance ever, or that a single sequence can only ever have one possible fold: both oversimplify documented exceptions.
origin: Demonstrated experimentally by Christian B. Anfinsen in 1961 using ribonuclease A; he was awarded the 1972 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (with Stanford Moore and William H. Stein) for the work.

sources.text: Anfinsen’s dogma, Wikipedia. — the statement, Anfinsen’s ribonuclease work, and documented exceptions.
"Christian B. Anfinsen," Encyclopaedia Britannica. — his 1972 Nobel Prize for the sequence-to-structure relationship.
